title: Matching identical findings by count
description: Two identical `_ = checkpanic getResult();` lines get the same hash (:1, :2). Matching uses the hash and the number of entries, never the occurrence number: with k entries, the first k unsuppressed findings in source order are baselined and the rest are new; with more entries than findings, the entries with the highest numbers are stale. The same line in another function is the same finding. A replacement (one removed, one added) is not detected; BEP 1498 documents this. Needs scan 0.15.0+.
upstream: BEP 1498: Finding fingerprints and baseline adoption (ballerina-spec/beps/tool-scan/1498_scan_baseline.md)

steps.name: Scan: 3 identical, 2 entries
steps.note: 1 new issue(s), 2 in baseline. The last one in source order (:3) is printed as new, whichever line was added; exit 1 from [gate].

steps.name: Scan: same line in another function
steps.note: The enclosing function is not hashed: still the same hash, so 1 new (the one in later(), last in source order).

steps.name: Scan: 1 identical, 2 entries
steps.note: 0 new issue(s), 1 in baseline, and 1 stale entry (the one with the highest number, :2, whichever line was removed).

steps.name: Scan: a replacement
steps.note: Known limitation: the count is unchanged, so the added finding is unchanged and nothing is stale. Exit 0.

steps.name: Scan: 2 identical, 1 entry
steps.note: 1 new issue(s), 1 in baseline: the second line (:2) is new again.
